page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.large is an instance within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. The server is provisioned with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at 3.1 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 22 MB L3 cache. It includes 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no dedicated GPUs and features no local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is configured at 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Instruction set support features standard x86 extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, although modern vector expansions like AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-VNNI, and AMX are not available. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits modest overall throughput. Stress-ng returned scores of 1346.89 in single-core and 1789.49 in multi-core execution. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1076.0 and a multi-core score of 1279.0, with subtests such as Clang compilation scoring 1810.0 and ray tracing scoring 1500.0. PassMark metrics reflect a total CPU score of 2188.15 and a memory score of 1037.0, with database operations registering at 609.36.

Memory throughput reaches 100.02 GB/sec for small cached 16 KB read blocks, dropping to 9.96 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached reads and 9.61 GB/sec for uncached writes. Workload-specific benchmarks include Redis SET performance of 1.78 million operations per second, static web serving throughput of 1.49 GB/sec, single-threaded gzip compression at 23.13 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 8.86 GB/sec. Small language model inference on a 135M model demonstrated prompt processing speeds of 130.51 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 36.29 tokens per second.

Given its two-thread limit across a single physical core and standard baseline network interface, ecs.hfg5.large is suited for light general-purpose workloads, background processing, developmental environments, small web servers, and low-scale database or caching instances where high single-threaded performance or dense core counts are not critical.
